evidence.note: Consistently reports current cycle count against target ('3198 cycles, still too high. L=6 didn't get us below target'; '2553 cycles, correct operation'), showing sustained tracking of distance to 1250 across iterations.

Recognizes a whole line of attack has stopped paying off — 'using valu for the MUX tree saturates the vector ALUs and prevents <1250' — and pivots to an ALU-MUX approach, then reverts when it judges it unnecessary. Genuine plateau detection and course change (anchor 8).

Attributes deltas to specific changes and begins a per-resource breakdown: identifies a load-engine floor of 1536 cycles/block, notes '16 lanes took 2357 vs 11 lanes 2749', and decomposes a 1248-cycle block into ~69 cycles/round — approaching a quantitative ledger of where cycles go.
Recognizes diminishing returns and explicitly decides to submit at 2293/2357 rather than grinding further ('missed 1250 cycles... decided to submit as is'), acknowledging it could not close the gap.
Momentary loss of attribution: confused why L=16 still gave 14175 cycles, later realizing it had used the wrong builder — a lapse that keeps this below a clean 8.

reasoning: The agent sustained an accurate current-cycle-vs-1250 picture across the entire horizon, attributed cycle deltas to specific changes (vselect vs multiply_add, lane counts, the load-engine floor), and pivoted when the valu-MUX line stopped paying off rather than grinding — matching the level-8 description. It even started a per-round/per-resource decomposition (toward level 10) but never a fully sustained ledger, and it showed some circular L-tuning and a config-attribution slip at step 206, so it lands just below 8.
